messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Over 1,500 ft, nothing above an H.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Over 1,500 ft is a floor. 1500 * 0.3048 = 457 m. Nothing above an H, so H or smaller. No wind, rail, site, or landing number: 2 m/s, 1.5 m, sea level, 6 m/s.
2. Feasibility: 457 m is a low bar for an H. A G might also clear it, but an H has more margin if the fins have to grow. I will look up two H motors and pick the one that clears 457 m without a huge airframe.

2. Feasibility: H128W is class H, 177.8 N*s, 152.6 N, 1.16 s, 29 mm by 0.194 m, 0.2016 kg, and the only delay is 14 s. H180W is 233.7 N*s with only a 6 s delay, which would open the chute early. The H128 is enough for a 457 m floor. On a guessed 0.40 kg rocket, thrust-to-weight is 152.6 / (0.40 * 9.81) = 38.9. Ejection at 1.16 + 14 = 15.2 s, which should be after apogee.
3. Size: For 0.40 kg at 5 m/s the chute is 2 * 0.40 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.32 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.32 / 3.1416) = 0.64 m. I will use 0.70 m. Tube 0.038 m, mount 0.032 m. Fins on the large side because an H in the tail has been short of 1 cal with small fins.
4. Draft: Cardboard ogive 0.15 m on a 0.65 m cardboard tube, outer diameter 0.038 m, wall 1 mm. H128W with the 14 s delay, chute at ejection. Nose mass 0.015 kg. Three birch fins, root 0.12 m, tip 0.05 m, span 0.09 m, sweep 0.05 m, 3 mm. Sea-level defaults.

4. Check: The simulator gives 1005.2 m, well over the 457 m floor. Margin 1.58 cal at the rail and through the burn. Rail exit 36.8 m/s, thrust-to-weight 42.0, landing 3.8 m/s, chute at 15.3 s, and it reached the ground. Mass 0.37 kg. The 14 s delay opens after the 10.91 s apogee.
5. Fix: 1005.2 m clears the floor and the gates pass, so this is the rocket.
6. Uncertainty: 1005.2 m is far enough over 457 m that a heavier paint job still clears. Peak Mach is 1.04, just over sonic, and this run did not attach a drag warning, so I would not lean on the last 50 m. Cd 0.8 is what makes 3.8 m/s. The chute opens at 15.3 s already on the way down.
